hero.eyebrow: Desktop app for Windows and macOS
hero.h1: The AI agent for university administrative documents
hero.sub: From document to decision in minutes, not days. DocOps ingests, classifies, searches with citations, maps legal impact and drafts under Decree 30. Your staff always make the final call.
hero.meta: Version {version} · Windows 10/11 · macOS 13 or later · Free to download, activated with your institution key
hero.imageAlt: DocOps review screen: document list with expired legal references highlighted

pipeline.caption: Six steps; a person decides at the last one

flows.lead: Three flows for the administrative document lifecycle, sharing one knowledge base that grows with your institution.

f1.title: Ingest & classify
f1.desc: OCR for scans, seal and signature detection, extraction of number, date and issuing body. Automatic classification and routing into the repository.

f2.title: Search & Q&A
f2.desc: Ask in plain language across the whole repository. Every answer cites its sources and says "insufficient basis" instead of guessing.

f3.title: Impact & drafting
f3.desc: Map legal relationships, flag expired references, generate drafts on Decree 30 templates and check the format before signing.

w1.title: Hours down to minutes
w1.desc: Across ingest, search and drafting, repetitive work drops from hours of manual effort to a few minutes.

w2.title: Citations, always
w2.desc: Every answer names its source and warns as soon as a cited basis has expired.

w3.title: Institutional memory that stays
w3.desc: The repository and the legal relationship graph accumulate year after year and do not leave with staff turnover.

w4.title: Compliant with Decree 30/2020 on clerical work
w4.desc: Document format follows the national standard; a staff member always approves before issuance.

t1.title: People decide
t1.desc: A document stays pending until a staff member reviews, edits and approves it. AI never replaces that decision.

t2.title: Data on your machine
t2.desc: Original documents live on your computer. Each institution gets its own key and a fully separate workspace.

t3.title: Never used for training
t3.desc: The server only runs the AI steps and keeps no content after returning a result.

download.lead: Version {version}, released {date}. Free to download, activated with your institution key.
download.note: The current build is not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS ask for a one-time confirmation. The installation guide walks through "Run anyway" and "Open Anyway".

q1.q: What is an activation key and where do I get one?
q1.a: Agentra issues each institution a key in the form DOCOPS-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX that opens its own workspace. Install the app, choose "No key yet (new registration)" on the activation screen and send the request from inside the app, or email us with your institution name.

q2.q: Do I need an internet connection?
q2.a: Yes, for activation and for the AI steps: OCR, classification, search and drafting. Your documents still stay on your machine.

q3.a: On your computer. The server only runs the AI steps and keeps no content after returning a result. Agentra never uses institution data to train models.

q4.q: Why does Windows or macOS warn me during installation?
q4.a: The current build has no code-signing certificate yet, so the operating system asks for a one-time confirmation. The guide shows exactly where to click "Run anyway" on Windows and "Open Anyway" on macOS.

q5.q: How do I get new versions?
q5.a: No re-download needed. In the app open Settings, the Version tab, click Check for updates, then Download and install, then Restart to install.

q6.a: Downloading and installing is free. Pricing depends on how much your institution uses; contact us for a quote.

cta.h2: Ready to try DocOps at your institution?
cta.sub: Download the app, request a key right from the activation screen, and start reviewing your document repository today.

unsigned.title: The current build is not code-signed
unsigned.body: Windows shows "Windows protected your PC" and macOS shows "Apple could not verify". That is the normal procedure for unsigned software, not an error. The installation guides show exactly where to click "Run anyway" (Windows) and "Open Anyway" (macOS); you only do it once.

macos.title: Install DocOps on a Mac
macos.description: How to install DocOps on macOS: pick the build for your chip, drag to Applications, allow the first launch in System Settings, activate with your key and update inside the app.

windows.title: Install DocOps on Windows
windows.description: How to install DocOps on Windows 10/11: download the Setup file, get past the SmartScreen warning, run the installer, activate with your key and update inside the app.
